consulted.title: MFE Docker image build failing — apt 404 errors on Debian bullseye packages - Show & Tell - Open edX discussions
consulted.content:
MFE container is using Debian 11 Bullseye.

Debian 11 Bullseye reached LTS end-of-life on August 31, 2026 — only a few days ago. Debian officially says Bullseye is no longer receiving further security updates after August 31, 2026. Debian -- News -- Debian 11 Long Term Support reaches end-of-life [...] Your EOL diagnosis is right, though the specific failure is narrower than a stale index. bullseye-security’s Release file is still being served (dated Aug 31) and still advertises exactly the versions in your log (linux-libc-dev 5.10.262-1, libc-dev-bin 2.31-13+deb11u14, libperl5.32 5.32.1-4+deb11u5), while the matching pool .deb files already return 404. That’s why apt update succeeds and only the install step fails, and why --no-cache on a fresh instance reproduces it. [...] Two things that may help narrow it down: plain bullseye on Index of /debian is untouched (final point release, pool still intact), so only the security suite is affected. And that security Release carries Valid-Until: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 21:13:04 UTC, so shortly apt update itself will start failing on an expired Release rather than the install 404ing. archive.debian.org does not carry bullseye-security yet, so the usual repoint-to-archive recipe won’t cover it right now.

consulted.title: MFE Docker image build failing — apt 404 errors on Debian bullseye packages - Show & Tell - Open edX discussions
consulted.content:
MFE container is using Debian 11 Bullseye.

Debian 11 Bullseye reached LTS end-of-life on August 31, 2026 — only a few days ago. Debian officially says Bullseye is no longer receiving further security updates after August 31, 2026. Debian -- News -- Debian 11 Long Term Support reaches end-of-life [...] Your EOL diagnosis is right, though the specific failure is narrower than a stale index. bullseye-security’s Release file is still being served (dated Aug 31) and still advertises exactly the versions in your log (linux-libc-dev 5.10.262-1, libc-dev-bin 2.31-13+deb11u14, libperl5.32 5.32.1-4+deb11u5), while the matching pool .deb files already return 404. That’s why apt update succeeds and only the install step fails, and why --no-cache on a fresh instance reproduces it. [...] Two things that may help narrow it down: plain bullseye on Index of /debian is untouched (final point release, pool still intact), so only the security suite is affected. And that security Release carries Valid-Until: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 21:13:04 UTC, so shortly apt update itself will start failing on an expired Release rather than the install 404ing. archive.debian.org does not carry bullseye-security yet, so the usual repoint-to-archive recipe won’t cover it right now.
